note: Seeds of the pure-shell campaign. Matrices converted from K's grid-editor PNGs by scripts/png_to_matrix.py: red = 1, green = 2, first row = top row of the picture. PNG-to-sample mapping follows the figure order of chapters.docx Chapter 5 (ASSUMPTION, K confirms). Real-fold text is a paraphrase of chapters.docx Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 (the report calls green knit and red purl; the web UI classifier and the 13 Nov success used red = 1).

seeds.real_fold: Good puckering and folding; distinct two-wale TM axes; rounder folds; curvature attributed to curling. Count (1/20s, 2/20s, 3/20s Ne) changes feel and recovery, not fold height or natural folding tendency.
Folds as well as samples 1-3, but lower maximum height: the height of the repeat unit controls the lift.
Only mild puckering from curling; diagonal TM axis gives very mild folds that creases can ruin; weakest class.

seeds.sample: Sample 6 (Miura-ori derivative, Mohmmed et al., uneven repeat)
seeds.real_fold: Weaker folds that creases affect; wale-bound TM axis but the uneven pattern makes it ineffective; 3D folds formed regardless, lower than Batch A.
TM axis forms in the course direction; folds very weak and not sharp, no loop-length migration keeping them sharp; a good example of course-direction 3D fabric.
Course-direction TM axis; far weaker, blunt folds compared with the tilted (wale-wise) Miura-ori.
Weakest folds made; beautiful folds when artificially folded but they quickly disappeared; negative result.
Remarkable folds; best course-direction sample, folds still blunt; auxeticity proven in the cited paper.
Course-wise folds, not as notable as sample 10 but remarkable; auxeticity proven in the cited paper.
